Meet a tutor

Tutors meet students in person and on video, and every session starts from the draft the student brings rather than from a fixed lesson plan. A session can cover an essay, a lab report, a thesis chapter, a personal statement or a grant proposal, at any stage from notes to final polish.

Appointments are fifty minutes long and can be booked two weeks ahead. Walk-in hours run every weekday afternoon while classes are in session, and a student who arrives without a draft is still welcome to talk through an assignment prompt, a reading, or a plan for the first page.

Tutors come from every level of study and many departments, and several of them work in more than one language. They read for argument and organization before grammar, and they leave the writing itself in the hands of the student who brought it to the table.
